title: Dilation theorem for continuum quantum stochastic processes
authors: Jonáš Fuksa, Clara Wassner, Jens Eisert, Gregory A. L. White
abstract: Connecting mathematical formalism in open quantum systems to its underlying physics necessitates the notion of a dilation, a way to bridge stochastic dynamics with deterministic Schrödinger evolution on a larger space. Although dilations are well known in the literature for states, channels, and quantum combs, there is a substantial gap when it comes to the fully general setting of non-Markovian dynamics on a continuous interval. In an accompanying work, we introduce a continuous process tensor (cPT) framework wherein these processes are represented by vectors in multi-species bosonic Fock spaces of $L^2$ functions. This accommodates all multi-time statistics of a quantum system on an interval. Here, we present a corresponding dilation theorem and show that all cPTs can be approximated arbitrarily well by an explicit closed description with system and environment coupled by a bounded Hamiltonian. As well as its physical appeal and demonstrating completeness of the framework, we show that such regular representations actually underpin the formalism, defining a dense subspace of all cPTs that is easy to handle. This leads to a continuum-suitable version of Choi duality, and permits the rigorous treatment of continuum controls.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous mathematical framework for continuous quantum stochastic processes by introducing Continuous Process Tensors (cPTs) in a Fock space. The central achievement is proving a 'strong dilation theorem,' which shows that any physically relevant cPT can be approximated by a process governed by a standard, bounded system-environment Hamiltonian. This allows for the rigorous extension of concepts like Choi duality to the continuum.
main_problem: The paper addresses the mathematical challenge of connecting the operational description of open quantum systems (non-Markovian dynamics on a continuous interval) to a rigorous underlying physical description via the concept of a dilation.
main_result: They establish a 'strong dilation theorem' showing that general continuous process tensors (cPTs) can be approximated by a Process-Canonical Representation (PCR), which is defined by an explicit, bounded system-environment Hamiltonian.
method: The authors utilize the framework of Continuous Process Tensors (cPTs) represented in a multi-species bosonic Fock space and develop a continuum generalization of Choi duality using specialized maps (P and V).
model_or_system: The system involves open quantum dynamics between a system (S) and an environment (E). The dynamics are mathematically captured by cPTs, which generalize discrete Process Tensors (PTs) to continuous time intervals.
key_observables: The primary observables are the cPTs themselves, the Fock norm ($\|\Upsilon\|^2_\Gamma$), and the resulting probability distributions derived from process statistics.
important_parameters: The key parameters involve the time-dependent Hamiltonian $H(t)$ defining the PCR, and the approximation error $\epsilon$ in the $\Gamma$-norm.
main_assumptions: The main assumption is that the physical process can be approximated by a representation governed by a bounded Hamiltonian (the PCR), although they note that not all cPTs are exactly PCRs.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates that general cPTs can have discontinuous wavefunctions, but these can be approximated by a discrete picture with a single dilation, which then defines a smoothed cPT.
paper_structure: The paper builds from discrete Process Tensors (PTs) to continuous Process Tensors (cPTs) in a Fock space. It then introduces the Process-Canonical Representation (PCR) as a structured subset, proving that general cPTs can be approximated by PCRs (Theorem 1). Finally, it extends this structure to define a continuum version of Choi duality.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful mathematical toolset for analyzing open quantum systems, moving beyond Markovian assumptions by providing a rigorous, Hamiltonian-based description (the dilation) for complex, non-Markovian dynamics.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic of our main result (Theorem 1). (a) The class cPT contains processes with discontinuous wavefunctions; these cannot be exactly represented by any single dilation. (b) Nevertheless, we show that these can be arbitrarily approximated by first going to a discrete picture with a single dilation, and then (c) defining from that an appropriately smoothed cPT.
